title: Images got more ways to start
summary:
Image generation gained new models and reference-image workflows, while model routes, queues, and usage reporting became easier to work with.

Nanobanana and Seedream 4.0 joined image generation with prompt and reference-image support. The image editor now accepts up to four references for supported models, the API accepts multiple reference URLs separated by pipes or commas, and non-square requests give Nanobanana aspect-ratio guidance. Both new models were also added to Enter’s image listings.

By week’s end, `openai` used GPT-5 Mini, `openai-fast` used GPT-5 Nano, and seed-tier users could reach GPT-5 Chat through `openai-large` or `gpt-5-chat`. DeepSeek V3.1, Gemini with built-in search, and the `geminisearch` alias expanded the other options. Several Gemini and Vertex routing fixes accompanied those additions.

Registered free text and image services became callable without an API key. Paid requests gained session and positive-Pollen-balance checks, while cached responses are not charged. Enter added usage-based price calculation, and image responses gained headers identifying the model, user tier, and reported image-token usage.

A per-IP queue fix lets token-authenticated requests use their tier-based concurrency rather than starting only one request per interval. Nanobanana and Seedream queue intervals dropped from 45 to 30 seconds, with higher per-interval caps for Flower and Nectar users. Image-response handling also gained clearer outcomes for blocked or empty results.
